question: GQ-001
subject: the rights filter was rejecting books from 1611 on a wording technicality
how_i_got_here: one turn earlier I examined the same filter, found its 86% rejection rate CORRECT, and wrote down what would change my mind: "a bare-assertion bucket dominated by pre-1929 material". The next want-list produced exactly that.

the_finding.eighth_list: 15 of 2,761 bare-assertion items were pre-1929 — the filter was right
the_finding.ninth_list: 538 of 1,076 (50%) are pre-1929, ranging 1611-1928, including 1920s periodicals
the_finding.why_they_were_excluded: classifyRights sees only the rights STRING, so a 1611 book whose metadata says a plain "Public Domain" grades identically to a 1994 engineering text with the same string

the_fix: a new age-settled grade, applied where both the year and the grade are known. It upgrades ONLY bare-assertion, never "none" or "not-a-designation", and requires a finite year — no year means no upgrade.
why_a_new_grade_not_a_widened_one: the manifest still records exactly which evidence admitted each book; folding it into formal-designation would have erased that distinction

verified_both_directions.what_remains_in_bare-assertion: 1980s-2010s — 165 from the 2000s, 168 from the 1990s, exactly what the grade exists to catch
